tr: Do you have a pen? / Yes, here you go.
What time is it now? / Three o'clock.
Whose book is this? / It's mine.
Where are you going? / I'm going to the supermarket.
What do you want to buy? / I want to buy two books.
What does this shop sell? / Clothes.
Where are you? / I'm at home.
Are you a teacher? / Yes, I am.
Is that enough? / That's enough, thanks.
How many people are there? / Lots of people.
What would you like to drink? / A glass of water, please.
Is this shirt big? / It's a little big.
Have you eaten anything yet? / Not yet, I'm starving.
Good morning! / Good morning, Mrs. Chan!
This present is for you. / Thank you!
I'm sorry I'm late. / It's OK.
Thanks so much! / You're welcome.
Long time no see! How have you been? / Pretty good, and you?
Hello? / Hello, Grandma, it's me.
Where's your mom? / She's in the kitchen.
Do you have any brothers or sisters? / Yes, I have an older brother.
Where does your grandma live? / She lives in Hong Kong.
Who's that? / He's my friend.
What's your name? / My name is Mark, and you?
Where are you from? / I'm American, and I live in New York.
What are you learning? / I'm learning Cantonese.
May I ask your last name? / My last name is Chan.
How many pineapple buns would you like? / Two, please.
How much is this? / 25 dollars.
Do you have any small change? / No, I only have a hundred-dollar bill.
Do you take US dollars here? / No, you need Hong Kong dollars.
Where's the book? / On the table.
How many tickets did you buy? / I bought two tickets, let's go together!
How many of you are there? / Three.
Where's my phone? / In your bag.
How many in your party? / Two, please.
For here or to go? / To go, please.
Grandma, why don't we go for dim sum? / Sure, I want shrimp dumplings.
Check, please! / Sure, that's 120 dollars.
How much is this bag? / Two hundred dollars.
Two hundred is too much. Could you go a bit cheaper? / OK, a hundred and eighty, then.
What are you looking for, miss? / Thanks, I'm just looking.
Can I try on these pants? / Sure, go ahead.
Do you take credit cards? / Yes, and Octopus too.
Do you need a bag? / No bag, thanks.
What time is it now? / Half past three.
What day is it today? / It's Friday.
What time do you start work? / I start at nine and finish at six.
When's your birthday? / December 3.
What time are we meeting tomorrow? / Tomorrow at three in the afternoon.
Excuse me, where's the restroom? / Upstairs, then turn left.
Excuse me, how do I get to the MTR station? / Go straight, cross the road, and it's across from the bank.
Is the museum far? / Not far, it's a five-minute walk.
Hello, where are you? / I'm at the MTR station exit.
Excuse me, where is this? / This is Mong Kok.
Where to? / To the airport, please.
Driver, does this minibus go to Mong Kok? / Yes, hop on.
Have you ever been to Macau? / No, I've never been.
Where do I get off for the Peak? / Get off at the next stop.
Are you there yet? / Not yet, I'm on the MTR.
How long does it take to get to Tsim Sha Tsui by MTR? / About ten minutes.
What line of work are you in? / I'm a teacher. I teach English at a high school.
Do you speak English? / Yes, but not very well.
What do you want to learn? / I want to learn Cantonese so I can chat with my grandma.
Are you working today? / I don't have to work today. I'm resting at home.
Where do you study? / I study at the University of Hong Kong.
How are you doing? / I don't feel well. I want to go home and rest.
Have you taken your medicine? / Not yet, I'll take it now.
Doctor, I have a sore throat and a bit of a fever. / You've caught a cold. You need more rest.
Excuse me, could you help me? / No problem, what's wrong?
Are you OK? / I'm fine, don't worry.
How's the barbecued pork here? / Delicious!
Was the movie any good? / So-so.
How tall is your little brother? / He's taller than me.
How's this soup? / Too spicy, I need some water.
The weather's really nice today. / Yeah, how about going to the park?
I'm American, and you? / I'm from Hong Kong.
We're going for dim sum. Come with us! / Sure!
I'm not going today after all. / Why?
We're going to Sai Kung tomorrow. Are you coming? / Yes, what time?
She's getting married next month. You didn't know? / I really had no idea!
It's so late. How are you getting home? / I'm taking a taxi home.
Have you eaten, Mrs. Chan? / Yes, I have. And you?
How are you today? / I'm tired. I want to go to bed early.
Did you go shopping yesterday? / I didn't go. I rested at home.
Long time no see. How are you? / I'm fine, and you?
Have you ever been to Hong Kong? / I've been to Hong Kong, but I've never been to Macau.
Let's go eat together! / Sorry, I can't today. I don't have time.
Your cooking is delicious! / If you like it, have some more.
You're really good at this! / Oh, not really!
Your Cantonese is really good! / I'm still learning.
You speak Cantonese?! / A little.
You look lovely today! / Oh, not really!
You did a great job. / Thanks for saying so.
I couldn't have done it without you, thanks so much! / You're welcome.
Your home is beautiful! / Thanks, come on in and sit down.
You have beautiful handwriting. / Nah, it's just so-so.
You're really good! / You're great too!
How do I look today? / Very handsome!
This photo is from when I was little. / So cute!
I speak English, Chinese and Japanese. / You're so clever!
You're a good person. / Thanks for saying so.
How long have you two been going out? / Three months now.
You look beautiful tonight. / Thank you, you look very handsome too.
You have a lovely smile. / You're such a sweet talker!
You sing beautifully. / Really? Thanks!
I love talking with you. / Me too.
Are you free tonight? / Yes, why?
Want to have dinner together? / Sure, where shall we eat?
Can I get your number? / Sure, here you go.
I'd like to ask you out. / Sure, what time?
I like you. / I like you too.
Shall we go to a movie on Saturday? / Sure, what time?
You're the most beautiful person I've ever met. / Are you kidding me?
Shall we go for coffee? / Thanks, but I have a boyfriend.
I kind of like you. / Thanks, but we're better as friends.
Are you seeing anyone? Can I ask you out? / Sorry, I don't want to date right now.
I found a job! / Yay! Congratulations!
Did you take the key? / Oh no, I forgot it!
Mr. Chan is getting married next month. / Really? I didn't know!
This top is a thousand dollars. / No way! That expensive?
He says he isn't coming today. / Surely not, he said he'd come.
The bank is next to the supermarket. / Oh, I see, thanks a lot.
I have to work tomorrow. / Oh, I see. Next time, then.
Flats in Hong Kong are so expensive. / Exactly, they really are.
Let's go. / Wait a sec! I haven't put my shoes on.
He's singing and dancing in the street. / I can't watch!
Careful! / Ouch!
I have an exam tomorrow. / You can do it! You'll be fine.
I'm getting married! / Congratulations!
Want more rice? / I'm fine, that's enough, I'm full.
OK, see you tomorrow. / OK, that's it for now, bye!
Sorry, I'm so slow. / No worries, take your time.
Are you kidding? / It's true, honest! I speak Cantonese.
